National Election Studies
National Election Studies
Lokniti-CSDS has a long and illustrious history of conducting National Election Studies during the Lok Sabha elections. Unbroken since 1996, this tradition has emerged as a veritable wealth of data regarding the political and social attitudes and choices of the Indian citizen around the election time. Most studies on Indian politics today would be incomplete without the wisdom and insight that these National Election Studies have provided. Academicians, journalists, scholars and the general public would all find this as an inexhaustible and treasured source of empirical details about the subject of politics in the country. Interested researchers are encouraged to browse through the attachments below. They can then call upon the Data Unit at Lokniti to get access to specifics that interest them.

Lok
Sabha
As per the provision of Article 79 of Indian Constitution, the House of the People, the Lok Sabha is the lower House of the parliament. Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of the adult suffrage. The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.
